The corpus now contains 33 substantive findings across hardware, risk traceability, software, DMR/SOP, and regulatory dimensions. assignments.review_focus: Close the verification gap analysis for PT9L. Specifically: (1) Determine whether any verification or validation record in the DHF corpus confirms that the object-temperature mode accuracy tolerance of ±0.2 °C applied at 30 °C and 45 °C in software test plans is intentional and justified against the design-input specification (which requires ±0.2 °C only for ≥35 °C and ≤42 °C body-temperature range). (2) Determine whether any V&V record addresses Bluetooth-specific hazards or Bluetooth functional verification for PT9L, given that the Risk Management Report acknowledges Bluetooth transmission capability but no Bluetooth hazard verification evidence was found by the Risk Traceability Agent. (3) Determine whether the battery design-verification plan/report blood-pressure residue phrase (identified by Hardware Agent) appears in a pass/fail verdict section or only in a boilerplate/template section, and whether the overall battery verification record carries a signed pass verdict. (4) Identify whether any verification record explicitly references the PT9L-FXGB01 V2.0 risk report (rather than V1.0) as the controlling risk document for verification closure. (5) Confirm whether the IEC 60601-1 test report referencing software design document DN:PT9L-RJFA01 V1.0 (noted by Software Agent as absent from the evidence catalog) has any corresponding entry in the design output list or verification index.

Perform a cross-finding synthesis and escalation assessment across all completed agent runs (RUN-0002 through RUN-0006) to support final report assembly. Specifically: (1) Assess whether the IFT-prefixed document number on the active Risk Management Plan (IFT-FXJH01 vs. expected PT9L-FXJH01) constitutes a document-control nonconformance under the applicable SOP or whether it is a known legacy prefix with a documented transition record. (2) Assess whether the F0013 PT2L risk plan carrying a PT9L-series document number internally (identified by both Risk Traceability Agent and Regulatory Agent) represents a single root cause or two distinct nonconformances requiring separate corrective actions. (3) Assess whether the biocompatibility reports conducted on PT5 samples rather than PT9L samples are covered by any equivalence or shared-component justification in the DHF, or whether this constitutes an unmitigated gap for 510(k) and CE submissions. (4) Assess whether the operation guide reference to MDD rather than MDR for biocompatibility compliance is a live document in the controlled release set or a draft/historical artifact. (5) Identify any findings across all agent runs that, in combination, suggest a systemic document-control process failure (e.g., unsigned approvals appearing across risk, design output, and DMR documents simultaneously) that should be flagged as a systemic finding rather than individual point findings. (6) Confirm whether the dual ASTM E1965 version citation (1998:2016 and 1998:2023) appears in the same document or in different documents at different design stages, and whether any transition rationale document exists in the corpus.
